questions.stem: Which regulation protects personal data of EU residents regardless of where the organisation is located?
questions.explanation: GDPR applies to any organisation processing EU residents' personal data, even if outside the EU, establishing rights and breach notification obligations.

questions.stem: The data minimisation principle under GDPR requires:

choices.A: Collecting only data adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary for the stated purpose
choices.B: Minimising the number of employees with data access
choices.C: Storing data for the minimum legally required period
choices.D: Using the minimum encryption key length sufficient for data sensitivity

questions.explanation: GDPR Article 5(1)(c): collect only what you actually need for the stated purpose, do not collect data 'just in case'.

choices.A: An encrypted copy of the original
choices.B: A randomly generated placeholder with no exploitable value outside the token vault
choices.C: A hashed version of the original

questions.explanation: Tokenisation substitutes sensitive data with a token. A separate secure vault maps tokens to originals. Intercepted tokens have no exploitable value without vault access.

questions.stem: Data masking is primarily used for:

choices.C: Replacing sensitive production data with realistic fictional data for non-production environments

questions.explanation: Data masking enables development and testing with realistic data formats without exposing actual customer PII, financial records, or health data.

choices.A: How long backups take to complete
choices.B: Required encryption standards for data at rest
choices.C: Which data can be stored in cloud environments
choices.D: How long different data categories must be kept and when/how they must be securely destroyed

questions.explanation: Retention policies define minimum and maximum retention periods per data category, driven by business need and regulatory requirements, plus secure disposal methods.

questions.stem: DLP tools enforce data protection by:

choices.B: Monitoring and blocking transfers of sensitive data based on content inspection and policy rules
choices.C: Blocking all external email to employees
choices.D: Requiring authentication before any USB file copy

questions.explanation: DLP inspects data in motion, at rest, and in use, blocking sensitive content transfers that violate policy.

choices.B: Only information held by hospitals and pharmacies
choices.C: Any individually identifiable health information in any form, electronic, paper, or verbal
choices.D: Only information shared with insurance companies

questions.explanation: HIPAA PHI encompasses any individually identifiable health information in any medium held by covered entities and their business associates.

choices.A: All data to be encrypted before international transfer
choices.B: Citizens' right to access their personal data
choices.C: Data collected about a country's citizens to be stored and processed within that country's borders
choices.D: Data to be replicated across multiple geographic regions

questions.explanation: Data sovereignty refers to legal requirements that data be subject to the laws of the country where it was collected, often requiring local storage.

questions.stem: The right to erasure under GDPR allows individuals to request:

choices.A: Immediate deletion of all personal data from all systems
choices.B: Backup copies to be overwritten when data is updated
choices.D: Deletion of personal data under defined circumstances such as when it is no longer needed or consent is withdrawn

questions.explanation: GDPR Article 17 grants the right to request deletion when data is no longer necessary, consent is withdrawn, or other conditions apply.

questions.stem: A company salary spreadsheet would be classified as:
questions.explanation: Salary data is sensitive PII requiring restricted access. Public data is approved for external release; Internal is for general employee access; Confidential requires stricter controls.
